data.title: ‘Bitcoin winter is over,’ says Fidelity as its predicts a new 4-year bull market
data.description:
Bitcoin rallied by 6% on Friday and reclaimed $80K as crude oil prices slipped below $100 per barrel. This eased fears of oil-driven inflation, sparking a strong rebound across U.S equity and crypto markets. For Fidelity, however, BTC’s resilience also meant that it might be ready for its next bull market cycle run. 

Why Fidelity thinks Bitcoin winter is over

According to Jurrien Timmer, Fidelity’s Head of Global Macro, BTC has held above $60K for about a year.

For him, two signals have been flagged – The 1-year Bitcoin winter and BTC/gold correlation turning positive. Timmer said that these signals confirm a durable bottom and potential early innings into the next bull cycle run. 

That’s how long a typical Bitcoin winter lasts (1 year), so I’m sensing that a new 4-year cycle bull market is underway.

He added that the market is now in a ‘new secular regime of higher cost of capital.’ He is expecting the government to respond with ‘financial repression.’ In other words, the government will do anything possible to contain the rising bond yields, including printing money. 

Put differently, the inflation from U.S government intervention could trigger demand for scarce assets like Bitcoin and gold. 

Interestingly, Timmer’s macro bullish outlook for BTC also seemed to align with technical indicators on the price charts. 

Bitcoin reclaims key bull market cycle level

Bitcoin’s Friday move effectively closed above the 50-week Moving Average (MA). Here, it’s worth noting that a true breakout could be confirmed if the weekly candlestick also closes above the level. 

Analysts, including Galaxy Research’s Head of Research Alex Thorn, have been tracking this level to gauge the end of the bear market and the start of the next bull market run. Notably, a previous attempt to break above the 50-week MA was rejected in early September. 

Reacting to BTC’s 6% surge on Friday, Thorn noted, 

BTC is looking strong here as it trades over the 50-week moving average. Move looks real.

Trader Bob Loukas also echoed a similar bullish position, noting that clearing the May high of $82K could push BTC’s price to above $90K.  

Very good setup here for Bitcoin to smash through the May highs and confirm a new bull market.

However, he cautioned that failure to clear $82K could open another possibility of retesting the lows around $60K. And even in such a downside scenario, the 200-day MA and BTC short-term holder (STH) realized price (at $71K) would be expected to act as support levels. 

That said, institutional traders are currently betting on a 35% chance that BTC will reclaim $90K by December. However, for the $100K-psychological level, the chances have dropped to 18%. 

Final Summary

  • Fidelity believes that BTC winter is over after a year, and the next bull run could begin soon. 
  • Analysts expect the asset to reclaim $90K if it clears the summer high of $82K.

data.title: Top 9 VPNs of September 2026
data.description:
VPNs hide a user’s data traffic online and help protect it from third parties. Virtual Private Networks mask your IP address and encrypt data between your device and a trusted endpoint. This ensures that user privacy is protected and reduces exposure on public and shared networks.

VPNs help to prevent third parties from spying or accessing sensitive information, and since not all VPNs are the same, users need to find the right one that matches their requirements. Here are the top picks of the month:

1. Nord VPN

NordVPN is one of the most popular VPNs in the world and has more than 15 million users around the world. The platform intends to make the internet a better place by making comprehensive protection effortless and accessible.

It has grown over time into an all-in-one digital security app that protects millions of users every day. It is pro-privacy and secures users’ connections with the world’s fastest VPN to shield online activity from others.

2. Proton VPN

Proton VPN provides no data or speed limits and no ads, along with the same level of security and trustworthiness as the paid plans. The Proton VPN Plus helps you select a specific country or server and stream geo-blocked content while travelling internationally.

It is open-source, and anyone can examine the code and independently audited. The strict no-logs policy means that they do not save any user connection logs. A user’s private browsing history stays private and cannot be turned over to a third-party.

3. Express VPN

Express VPN gives users an all-in-one app for online privacy, security, and freedom. It has servers in over 113 countries and the best-in-class encryption. All connections are secured through AES-256, and it offers peak speeds of up to 1,177 Mbps as per independent testing.

The platform’s server runs entirely on RAM, so all data can be wiped clean with every reboot. Users can use up to 14 devices at a time; there is also a no-activity-logs policy. The VPN works on every platform through Windows, Mac, iOS, Android, and Linux.

4. Norton VPN

Norton VPN has an advanced privacy and malware protection program that lets users access their favourite content around the world. It is an easy-to-use VPN that automatically connects to the fastest country and lets you browse more securely.

The advanced protection allows you to safeguard online activity with an encrypted VPN tunnel and AI-powered protection against scams, phishing, and malware. It also has a no-logs policy so it does not track or log the websites users visit.

5. Surfshark VPN

Surfshark aims to empower users to take full control of their digital assets and raise awareness about evolving online threats. Surfshark offers not just a VPN but also an antivirus, alert, search, alternative ID, and number. The platform publishes its annual reports in order to maintain its credibility and transparency among users.

The VPN has a server network of more than 4500 servers across 100 countries and also has features like post-quantum encryption, built-in ad blocking, and multi-hop connections. Pricing depends on the plan that the user chooses and their region; usually, long-term subscriptions have the lowest rates.

6. Windscribe VPN

Windscribe’s mission is to make privacy accessible for everyone and make internet freedom a reality. They believe that the internet should be open and free of censorship, surveillance, and invasive tracking. The VPN is self-funded and does not track user data. The platform has a freemium model that lets anyone try it without pressure and relies on word of mouth to grow.

The VPN has 120+ cities with more than 224,951 connections and prioritizes privacy, security, and usability. The Pro version has broader server access, unlimited data, and features like multi-hop connections and residential IP options.

7. PIA VPN

Private Internet Access, or PIA, has a strict no-logs policy along with lightning-fast connection speeds. It has built a strong reputation centered around privacy and torrenting. It is also open-source, adding an extra layer of transparency for users.

There are also features like port forwarding, an integrated ad blocker called MACE, and anonymous payment options for users who want a little more privacy. It also has one of the largest server networks in the space, with more than 18,000 servers spread across 91 countries.

8. Mullvad VPN 

Mullvad VPN is a privacy-focused VPN that hides users’ IP addresses and encrypts their internet traffic. It allows for traffic encryption and routes users’ connections through a secure tunnel using the WireGuard protocol, along with a no-logs policy.

Users are assigned a random account number upon signing up instead of using their email. The apps are open-sourced for anyone who wants to take a closer look at the software. There are also some advanced privacy tools aimed at reducing AI-based traffic tracking.

9. Hide.me 

Hide.me has a VPN service that offers both free and paid options. It has dynamic port forwarding where users can automatically open necessary ports, ensuring seamless connections for games, P2P, and more. It has multihop double VPN, meaning that users can tunnel their connection over multiple VPN locations, and users can pick an entry and exit server.

The SmartGuard ad blocker lets users navigate the web with a trusted ally and proactively guards against malware, tracking ads, and phishing threats. There is also a split tunnelling option, and it has over 2600+ servers in over 92 locations.

Final word 

VPNs have become an essential part of the internet browsing experience. It is a simple and effective way to improve online privacy and ensure secure internet connections while browsing. It should be combined with trusted security software for an extra layer of protection.

Users should use their own discretion and research before getting their own VPN.

data.title: Predicting Starknet’s next short-term price target after STRK hits 4-month high
data.description:
The altcoin market is in the middle of a trend reversal right now after a period of prolonged weakness. Starknet is no exception to the same. In fact, after STRK successfully held $0.03, the altcoin hiked and flipped $0.04, before hitting $0.046. In doing so, it reached its May 2026 levels.

At the time of writing, STRK was trading at $0.040 following a hike of 31% on the daily charts. Its trading volume saw a record-breaking jump too, with the same up by a whooping 718%. This hinted at greater market participation across the board. 

Here, it’s worth noting that this market activity seemed to be mostly on the buy side. Coinank data revealed that Daily Turnover had jumped to a yearly high of $6.6 million, hinting at greater buying pressure.

A look at Starknet’s recovery

As the market rebounded, Starknet [STRK] investors returned with strength. On 18th September, for instance, the protocol’s capital inflows climbed to $61.7 million.

USD Inflows on Starknet Bridge have not hit these levels since November 2025. Previously, when protocol inflows were hitting such a level, STRK was on a strong upside run while trading at around $0.28.

On top of that, open market demand also seemed to echo this market shift. In fact, over the past 4 days, the altcoin’s Spot Netflows have remained negative.

On 19th September, Netflows dropped to -$1.34 million for the first tume since April. A look at both USD inflows and exchange flows revealed that when both reached press time levels previously, Starknet performed well on the price charts.

Is there reason to worry though?

Despite growing market optimism and capital flows, the crypto community has some concerns with STRK. Especially since some on-chain monitors have raised concerns over team-linked wallet dumping. 

According to Arsian, over the past month, team-linked wallets have sold every time the token recorded some gains. In its latest move, team-linked wallets received 17 million STRK and started depositing to exchanges.

At first , the wallet deposited 4 million STRK into Binance. Often, these deposits have followed dumping based on previous patterns. Such market behavior, especially from the team, tends to increase supply, which also precedes market weakness.

Additionally, new supply is anticipated to hit the market, according to Miau. The analyst noted that 175M tokens will likely increase new supply, resulting in a new fight between renewed demand and fresh supply.

These two aspects are likely to cause market pressure and risk the prevailing trend’s sustainability.

Can STRK hold the uptrend?

Regardless of the highlighted concerns, the market was leaning bullish at press time. STRK’s price was sitting above its short-term and long-term moving averages, reflecting strong upside pressure.

At the same time, Starknet’s Relative Strength Index (RSI) sat deep in the bullish zone at around 66.

Together, these trend indicators hinted at the likelihood of a trend continuation. Therefore, if the demand can hold, STRK will reclaim $0.046 and target a flip of $0.05. For this outlook to hold, STRK must close above $0.041. Failure to do so, and the altcoin could revisit $0.03 support.

Final Summary

  • Starknet [STRK] surged by 31% and flipped $0.04-resistance to hit a four-month high of $0.046.
  • Starknet’s rally driven by strong market demand and improving market sentiment.

data.title: President Trump or Coinbase’s Armstrong — Who’s really responsible for CLARITY Act failure?
data.description:
Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong has distanced himself from claims by the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) that he was responsible for the CLARITY Act’s failure. 

The much-awaited and crucial crypto legislation hit a snag earlier in the week after it failed to clear a procedural vote to advance to the Senate floor debate. 

No Democrats supported the bill, citing limited ethics provisions. A handful of Republicans also withheld support, bringing the vote tally to 49 (Yes)-50 (No), which fell short of the 60 votes needed to advance the bill.

However, the WSJ is reportedly planning to pin the failure on Armstrong. In response, Armstrong stated, 

In January, I opposed a draft of the bill going into a committee vote because it needed a lot of work on DeFi, tokenization, CFTC authority, and stablecoin rewards. At the time, the bill had major issues that would have harmed crypto.

At the time, even the White House scolded his opposition and warned that he’s not the crypto industry. However, he insisted that he’s “proud” of his opposition because it led to a “better bill.”

On the revised version, which had a stablecoin yield compromise, Armstrong added, 

The final draft of CLARITY that went to the Senate was great, and I strongly supported it. It’s a shame that the WSJ takes direction from bank lobbyists.

On the contrary, some industry insiders blamed Trump’s $1.4B crypto profits as largely responsible for the ethics stand-off and the bill’s failure. 

SEC, CFTC advance crypto clarity via rulemaking

Here, it’s worth pointing out that the bill stalled on Tuesday. However, by Thursday, the regulators (SEC and CFTC) had begun rolling out rulemakings. 

Notably, the CFTC issued no-action relief for passive software providers, effectively allowing players like self-custodial wallets such as Phantom to avoid registering as brokers to offer derivative trading. 

Additionally, the CFTC submitted a new crypto market structure proposal for White House review. If approved, it would allow existing and unregistered crypto platforms to get approval for leveraged trading. This is the regulated pathway that Hyperliquid is betting on to gain U.S market entry. 

Separately, the SEC also made similar moves. It published a 5-year tokenization exemption program, allowing crypto platforms to facilitate tokenized stock trading. This would exempt some firms from registering as full securities exchanges. 

Still, the rulemaking approach can be reversed by the next administration if the rules aren’t codified by Congressional legislation. For his part, ETF expert Nate Geraci views the rulemaking as a “legitimate window” for the crypto industry to build. 

However, others believe that there are still regulatory risks for investors and developers if the next regime is anti-crypto. 

Final Summary

  • Coinbase CEO slammed WSJ for linking him to the CLARITY Act’s failure. 
  • Analysts are split on regulatory risks associated with SEC and CFTC’s rulemakings.

data.title: XRP vs Solana vs Cardano — Which altcoin will have the best September?
data.description:
Altcoin leverage remains below its risk threshold, according to crypto market intelligence platform Glassnode in a post on X.

When the altcoin market’s Open Interest comes to within a few percentage points of Bitcoin’s [BTC], the altcoin market can be considered overextended. As it stands though, these conditions are far from being met.

Now, some of the market’s most popular leading alts, Solana [SOL], Cardano [ADA], and Ripple [XRP], have had bullish runs in recent weeks. Which of them has the potential for the best returns for the rest of September?

All three alts showcase a bullish structure

Solana’s daily structure was flipped bullishly when the $98.41-swing level was breached. In recent weeks, SOL saw rejection from the $110-resistance area and briefly fell below $100.

The bulls were able to defend the $95-$100 demand zone and drove prices higher. The next resistance to watch is at $119.6, a former support turned resistance from late 2025.

Cardano has also been on a bullish run since its structure shift in July. The altcoin has set a series of higher highs since then. The retracement earlier this week saw ADA retest the $0.19-support level.

The reaction from there has been encouraging though, and Cardano may be primed to challenge the $0.23 and $0.255 resistance levels.

Like the other two, XRP also had a bullish structure at press time. Unlike the other two though, XRP was pushing into a long-term supply zone that has repeatedly driven the bulls back.

For this reason, it is possible that XRP would struggle to be the most bullish token among the three for the rest of the month.

Is Solana’s run done?

Solana has recorded the highest returns since Wednesday, around 16%, compared to 14% and 11% for Cardano and XRP. Additionally, only Solana has managed to breach the highs set towards the end of August, when Bitcoin began to pull back and dragged the altcoin market down with it.

This seemed to indicate that XRP and ADA have room to catch up to SOL, making them likely to return greater profits this month. And yet, it is Solana that has proven bullish momentum by making new local highs.

Therefore, so long as Bitcoin does not suffer a steep pullback, the leading altcoin among the trio, SOL, is likely to continue to register better returns.

Final Summary

  • Altcoin market leverage was relatively low compared to BTC’s Open Interest, indicating that altcoins still have room to make gains.
  • Among Solana, Cardano, and XRP, SOL appeared the most likely to continue its strong bullish momentum.

data.title: Raydium’s 26% rally cools down below $1.80 — Is downside liquidity calling for RAY?
data.description:
Raydium rallied on the price charts as the broader cryptocurrency market saw green across the board.

In this case, the timing was particularly interesting. Especially since it followed Injective’s Solana expansion which strengthened RAY’s fundamentals. To be specific, Injective’s Solana launch introduced another potential source of trading activity for Raydium’s decentralized exchange.

Reportedly, Raydium joined the rollout as a day-one liquidity partner, granting Injective assets immediate access to Solana blockchain liquidity.

Here, it is also important to note that Raydium accounts for over 90% of memecoin DEX trading volume on Solana. In fact, its cumulative tokenized stock volume recently surpassed $5 billion on the blockchain.  

The aforementioned integration will also enable participants to trade Injective ecosystem tokens through Raydium, eventually funneling additional swaps and liquidity.

For its part, RAY’s price gained by 15.19% over 24 hours. Its trading volume simultaneously surged by 125.5% too, hinting at greater market participation. 

Are retail traders on board with RAY?

While the altcoin’s price action did surge, so did the retail Futures activity. This pushed trading frequency into the “Too Many Retail” area. In fact, this metric’s reading implied that smaller traders increasingly entered Futures trading as RAY’s price pushed higher.

Furthermore, the 90-day Futures Taker CVD also maintained taker-sell dominance across the derivatives market.

Therefore, aggressive sellers likely started taking in profits after RAY’s sharp price appreciation.

Hence, retail traders chased the rally while taker activity revealed persistent selling. Taken together, these findings might imply possible exhaustion after the rapid price expansion.

What happened after RAY swept its swing high?

On the 24-hour chart, Raydium’s [RAY] price rally extended by roughly 26.16%. Thanks to the same, it briefly hit the $1.85 swing high, before a retracement on the charts. 

Notably, the move above previous highs appeared to grab nearby internal liquidity instead of establishing $1.85 as resistance. Subsequently, the price then slipped below the $1.80-resistance level, with the token trading at around $1.77 at press time. 

The MACD indicator remained supportive after crossing above its Signal line. Furthermore, its positive histogram reading of 0.0341 suggested that the bullish pressure had not fully faded after the retracement. 

The RSI indicator, however, breached 72.27, placing the token in overbought conditions. 

Ultimately, reclaiming the $1.80-resistance would be crucial for an upside continuation. A sustained rejection, however, could instead reinforce the pullback as price gravitates towards denser lower liquidity.

Downside liquidity strengthens pullback risk

With reference to the technical price structure, RAY’s latest rally may have already collected much of the nearby upper liquidation liquidity. Attention can now shift towards the substantially denser liquidation concentrations below the press time price.

Notably, the strongest visible clusters can be seen around the $1.64–$1.66 region. All while the taker-sell dominance and overbought RSI conditions increased the significance of a rejection around the $1.80-area.

Persistent rejection around that key level could therefore push RAY towards the $1.64–$1.66 liquidity pool before another sustained recovery attempt.

However, such a correction would not invalidate the broader structure while $1.2202 remains protected.

Final Summary

  • Injective strengthened Raydium’s growth narrative, but Futures sellers challenged the rally.
  • RAY lost $1.80 after its daily swing-high sweep, increasing near short-term price correction risk.

data.title: Polygon to burn 100M POL as revenue hits $24.5M, but will this help the token?
data.description:
Polygon is prepping for the next crypto market bull cycle with an aggressive POL deflationary plan. In a post on X on Friday, Polygon Foundation CEO Sandeep Nailwal announced the project will permanently burn 100M POL tokens, citing impressive protocol revenue.  

Polygon is printing revenue. $24.5m YTD. We are deploying a change that lets anyone in the community trigger its burn.

Nailwal noted the proposal is now awaiting the final Security Council sign-off to be implemented. Following the same, there will be manual quarterly burns. 

Polygon’s base fees add POL to its collector wallet.

According to Nailwal, the collector currently holds 121M POL, worth about $1.2M. If the 100M tokens are burnt as planned, that will remove 1% of POL circulating supply from the market.  

Will Polygon’s burns boost POL’s value?

Polygon has aggressively repositioned itself for payments, especially stablecoin-based transfers. According to Nailwal, the traction and the generated fees are now 3x that of Arbitrum and 5x that of Near Protocol. 

In fact, according to DeFiLlama, Polygon’s collected annual revenue crossed $25M too, marking a two-year high. 

Whether the traction will hold steady in the coming months and fuel POL’s burn rates remains to be seen though. 

In the meantime, POL’s price surged by 10% on the 100M token burn update. The altcoin had initially rallied +80% from $0.07 to $0.11 in Q3, before a sharp pullback in late August. It spent September consolidating above the $0.09 support (which doubles as the 200-day Moving Average, blue). 

The Friday pump was part of the token’s weekly 20% recovery gain as Bitcoin reclaimed $80K. The 100M token update also boosted the move. 

There may still be room for POL’s recovery to extend because the daily RSI was yet to hit overbought territory at press time. However, the ATR (Average True Range) was flat, signaling low volatility. 

This implied that a strong breakout above $0.11 might remain elusive in the short term. Here, it’s also worth pointing out that the $0.11-level was also the 50-week Moving Average (MA) that blocked the explosive August rally.  

Interestingly, key whale wallets dumped over 30M POL in the last three days, which could further stall the rally as the sell-off persists. 

If POL stalls again at the dynamic resistance (near $0.11), a retest of the $0.09-support could not be ruled out. On the contrary, clearing the $0.11 overheld hurdle may mark the next leg of its recovery. 

Final Summary

  • Polygon Foundation CEO Sandeep Nailwal announced that 100M POL tokens will be burned, subject to Security Council approval.
  • The mid-week 20% recovery rally soon attracted whale profit-taking.

data.title: Midnight prepares open smart contract deployment on mainnet: Details
data.description:
Midnight seems ready to activate the much-awaited smart-contract support for the privacy-focused blockchain. 

In an X post on Saturday, Sebastien Guillemo, the CTO of Midnight Foundation, said that the upgrade will soon be rolled out on the mainnet and will include private smart contracts. 

Initially, only a few decentralized applications on Midnight such as AscendPerps were whitelisted, allowing them to run in a gated garden. However, the latest update means that smart contract support will be available for anyone to experiment with and deploy. 

The blockchain runs as a sidechain to Cardano, but leverages zero-knowledge (ZK) proofs for its underlying privacy architecture. In fact, the blockchain has been billed as a solution for institutional players seeking on-chain. 

That’s exactly why the private smart contracts feature and the ability to mint private tokens (think of a Zcash-like token) have attracted growing interest in the network. 

Additionally, Guillemot noted that the next version of smart contracts will come with extra features, including events and composability. 

In other words, it will allow the development of DeFi apps that can communicate with each other, ideally allowing complex apps such as the Aave lending protocol. 

Will privacy narrative fuel Midnight’s adoption?

Midnight went live in Q1 2026, and the latest announcement is part of its transition into open deployment and decentralization. 

Commenting on the same, Dave, a Cardano DRep (delegated representative), said, 

Good progress from the Midnight team. The privacy stack is starting to move from architecture into usable infrastructure, and that is where things get interesting, a huge milestone for Midnight.

That said, the privacy narrative has been one of the strongest metas, alongside perps, prediction markets, and stablecoins. 

In fact, according to trader Bob Loukas, the privacy coins segment didn’t even “experience a crypto bear market” given their strong performance as other tokens dumped hard.  

Privacy coins didn’t experience a bear market this cycle. Not sure we can say that about any token over the prior cycles. That’s telling, and it’s more than just a narrative imo.

It’s now a question of whether the strong traction of the privacy segment will spill over to NIGHT, Midnight’s native token. 

The token has pumped by 30% this week, but it hit the upper range of its ascending channel. If the pattern persists, the channel’s range lows and highs could offer trading opportunities like it did over the past few days. 

Final Summary

  • Midnight has announced plans for smart contract support on the mainnet. 
  • NIGHT jumped by 30% this week, but whether it will ride the privacy coins narrative is unclear.

data.title: All about SKY’s price rally and if $569M in TVL growth will overshadow spot selling
data.description:
Sky Protocol [SKY] recorded significant gains over the last 24 hours, with the altcoin gaining by 14% on the charts. However, while these gains appeared to be strongly bullish, they have relied significantly on sentiment.

CoinMarketCap Sentiment, which uses a scale between -10 and 10 to measure investors’ outlook for an asset, highlighted a mildly bullish outlook for SKY. According to the same, it had a reading of 1.96, suggesting that investors are likely to accumulate more of the asset without the expectation of going all out.

Worth pointing out, however, that SKY’s perpetual market activity has been supporting these price gains too, with capital flows and positions pointing to further upside.

Capital flow and positions fuel bullish odds

SKY’s perpetual market revealed that there has been some growth in its capital base.

According to Coinglass, the Open Interest surged by 27% to hit roughly $39 million at press time. A surge in the capital base is a reflection of investors’ outlook for the asset, likely determining whether the asset trends higher or eventually sees a decline.

The Funding Rate, which tracks the cost of holding perpetual positions, rose too and pointed to growing long positioning in the market.

Are Spot traders selling?

Over the past three days, there has been an established selling trend among traders in the Spot market. In fact, there has been a cumulative sell-off of $363,000. This trend seemed to be even more visible over the last 24 hours, with Netflows of approximately $788,000.

For context, positive Netflows mean more SKY is moving into exchanges for sale than out of exchanges into private wallets for long-term holding.

As it stands, the primary concern stems from the divergence between Spot and Perpetual Market positioning.

In a typically sustained bull market, there tends to be bullish positioning from both the Spot and Perpetual Markets without overbought conditions. Spot would need to begin accumulating before the trend can be confirmed as fully supportive of a sustained bull market.

What do on-chain indicators tell us?

Finally, activity in the on-chain market has been fairly relaxed, without any major significant growth in market activity.

For instance, DeFiLlama reported that SKY’s Total Value Locked (TVL) has maintained a steady path with no significant gains or drops until 17th September. On that day, it added $569 million.

This growth, however, did not coincide with the fees generated as they held steady over the past day. Simply put, the price is now likely to continue its uptrend if market activity still supports it.

Final Summary

  • SKY gained by 14% as Open Interest climbed by 27% to $39 million.

  • Spot traders recorded $363,000 in cumulative selling over three days, creating a divergence between Spot and Perpetual market activity.

data.title: Can Ethereum turn Friday’s price rally of 6.5% into a sustained breakout?
data.description:
Ethereum [ETH] surged by 6.5% in the last 24 hours to trade at $2,618.67 at press time. This is a level the altcoin last saw back in January 2026. The timing here is interesting since the global cryptocurrency market cap also climbed to $2.88 trillion following gains of 4.6%. 

What is also interesting is that the said recovery followed several developments that would normally put significant pressure on risk assets.

For context, over the past week, the CLARITY Act failed to advance in the Senate and the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points. Additionally, the Bank of Japan also raised rates while the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) moved back above 100 and and oil prices increased.

Not just a price playdate

And yetm Ethereum saw a surge in whale transactions. This, and its holder base, continued to expand, with a record 207.17 million non-empty wallets. Staking is another major factor that has supported long-term ETH demand.

With more than 40 million ETH currently staked, there has been a significant removal of ETH from immediately available market supply. 

At the same time, Ethereum has remained a major hub for decentralized finance (DeFi), securing roughly $50 billion in TVL across lending platforms, decentralized exchanges, stablecoin applications and liquid-staking protocols. 

Finally, ETH ETFs also flipped the three-day outflow streak with $143.7 million in inflows. 

Other altcoins also surfed the bullish momentum

Needless to say, besides Ethereum, Bitcoin [BTC] moved back above $80,000, while several major altcoins recorded more significant gains.

For instance, Solana [SOL] and Hyperliquid [HYPE] hiked by more than 10% and Uniswap [UNI] gained by around 16%.

Is there still some uncertainty around?

However, not everything may be as rosy as it seems. The Ethereum Foundation transferred approximately $2.45 million worth of ETH to an unlabeled Gnosis Safe, a type of smart contract wallet commonly used for managing funds collectively or securely.

Now, because the receiving wallet is unlabeled, it is not yet clear whether it is directly controlled by the Ethereum Foundation or belongs to another entity.

The transfer, therefore, does not necessarily mean that the foundation is selling ETH or reducing its holdings. This, because on-chain data reportedly shows that the Foundation still holds around $235.46 million worth of ETH and $23 million in USDC.

Final Summary

  • Ethereum’s recent gains were recorded despite several negative developments that would have impacted its bullish momentum.
  • Besides ETH and BTC, several altcoins saw massive surges, with some seeing weekly hikes of over 45%.
